sections.text: Employees receive 18 days of paid annual leave per calendar year.
Leave requests should be submitted at least five working days before the planned start date.
Unused annual leave can be carried forward for up to five days into the next calendar year.
Employees may work remotely up to two days per week with manager approval.
Roles requiring on-site equipment access may have different remote-work arrangements.
Employees must report suspected phishing emails to security@example.test.
Employees must never share passwords with colleagues or support staff.
Business travel expenses must be submitted within 30 calendar days after the trip ends.
Receipts are required for individual expenses above 25 currency units.
New employees must complete security awareness training within 14 calendar days of their start date.
Company laptops must use full-disk encryption.
Company laptops must lock automatically after five minutes of inactivity.
Suspected loss of a company device must be reported to the IT service desk immediately and no later than one hour after discovery.
Agendas should be shared at least one working day before meetings longer than 30 minutes.
Software purchases costing more than 500 currency units require department-head approval before purchase.
Employees should use the approved booking portal for business travel.
Employees must report workplace safety concerns to their manager or the safety team.
Official records must be stored in the approved document repository.
New employees receive an onboarding checklist from Human Resources.
Internal support requests should include a short description, impact, and preferred contact method.
Production databases are backed up every night at 02:00 UTC.
Production database backups are retained for 30 days.
A restore request must include the database name, requested recovery point, business justification, and approving service owner.
The internal status page is status.example.test.
The incident commander posts major incident updates every 30 minutes.
Production deployments are paused on Fridays after 15:00 UTC unless an emergency change is approved.
Privileged access uses time-limited approvals and must be reviewed every 90 days.
Application logs are retained for 14 days.
Security audit logs are retained for 180 days.
A critical database alert must be acknowledged within 10 minutes.
Escalate a critical database alert if unresolved after 15 minutes.
Every production change must have a rollback plan.
Every production change must have a named owner and a linked change ticket.
Secrets must be stored in the approved secret manager.
Secrets must not be committed to source control.
The sample API has a 99.9% monthly availability objective.
The on-call engineer is the escalation contact for unresolved critical alerts.
Major incidents must have a named incident commander.
Emergency changes require an approving incident or change owner.
Logs should not contain passwords, access tokens, or full document contents.
The demo application accepts PDF and DOCX files.
Files larger than 25 MB are rejected by the demo upload endpoint.
The chat endpoint supports streamed responses.
The client should display citations when the backend returns source metadata.
Conversation history is scoped to the authenticated user.
Changing a session identifier must not grant access to another user's history.
Deleting a document should remove it from the listing.
Deleting a document should invalidate cached answers that depend on it.
Evaluation runs should record dataset version, configuration, model identifiers, metrics, and timestamp.
Cache keys should include the authenticated user's access context.
Cache keys should include the index version.
A citation must refer to retrieved evidence.
A user must be authorized to access a cited source.
Logs should avoid storing full document contents.
Logs should avoid storing access tokens, passwords, or unnecessary personal data.
The health endpoint must not expose credentials or environment secrets.
The health endpoint must not expose private document text.
Protected API routes require a valid authenticated session.
Uploaded documents must be associated with the authenticated user's account.
The streaming client must handle partial chunks and a clean end-of-stream event.
Invoices should include a supplier name, invoice date, and invoice number.
Invoices above 2,000 currency units require finance-manager approval.
Approved invoices are scheduled for payment within 15 business days.
Meal reimbursement is capped at 40 currency units per travel day.
Department budgets are reviewed quarterly.
New vendors must pass the standard vendor review before payment.
Tax-related records must be retained for seven years.
Receipts must be attached to expense claims when available.
Foreign-currency expenses must include the original amount and conversion rate.
An approver must not approve their own expense claim.
Refund requests require the original transaction reference.
Month-end close tasks should be completed by the fifth business day.
Purchase orders must be created before a non-emergency purchase.
Finance approvals must be recorded in the audit trail.
Bank reconciliations are performed monthly.
Petty cash transactions require a dated receipt.
International travel requires manager approval before booking.
Budget owners must explain variances greater than 10 percent.
Duplicate invoices should be flagged before payment.
Vendor bank-detail changes require independent verification.
Pull requests require at least one approving reviewer.
New business logic should include automated tests.
The continuous integration pipeline runs linting and unit tests.
A release candidate must pass required CI checks before release.
Services must document a rollback procedure.
Public API changes must be documented.
Dependency updates should be checked for known vulnerabilities.
API keys must not be stored in source code.
Feature branches should be rebased or merged regularly.
Behavior-changing configuration options must be documented.
Performance regressions should be measured against a recorded baseline.
Customer-impacting incidents require a post-incident review.
Services should expose health and readiness checks.
Schema migrations must include a rollback or recovery plan.
Review comments should identify the issue and a suggested improvement.
Critical regression tests should run in CI.
Breaking API changes require a versioning strategy.
Authentication and authorization must be checked server-side.
Cache invalidation behavior must be tested after source updates.
Each production service must have a named owning team.
